<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="QA customer stories 848-853">
Run per-story QA sessions SEQUENTIALLY in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm for the six NEW customer-side stories: 848 (instant quote), 849 (accept & book), 850 (client portal), 851 (reschedule/cancel), 852 (pay + tip), 853 (reviews). You are the ONLY browser driver — do NOT delegate to sub-agents (browser tools are scoped to your session).

MCP notes: on "No session_id available" errors add explicit session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8". If MCP hangs >2 min, message me and wait; timeouts often commit server-side — verify with a read before re-writing.

Per story: start_task (requirement_name="qa_complete", entity_type="story", entity_id="<id>") → write the brief → execute in the browser → create_issue for real defects AS FOUND → submit_qa_result (non-pass REQUIRES issue ids) → MESSAGE ME the verdict before the next story. ~35 browser actions/story; submit early over perfect.

App facts: http://127.0.0.1:4100 — detached OTP release (stable; NEVER start servers; the ONLY mix command allowed is `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`; message me if anything's down or you need another command run). Owner qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / "qa password 1234"; cleaner qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / same. psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev for persistence checks and token harvesting. Stripe = Test adapter (dev); /webhooks/stripe accepts unsigned JSON payloads (payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed with the payment intent id from psql). Confirm dialogs are DaisyUI modals ([data-role='confirm-confirm']). Selects that don't fire events: browser_evaluate set .value + dispatch input/change bubbles:true. Trap JS errors via window.onerror.

CUSTOMER-SIDE surfaces (all new, unauthenticated unless noted):
- /book — public instant-quote calculator (bedrooms/bathrooms/sqft/frequency/add-ons → live price from the owner's rate card, frequency discount shown, trust signals; contact captured AFTER price). Rate cards are managed by the owner under /quotes (existing surface) — ensure one exists (seeds or create via owner UI).
- /book/accept/:token — acceptance: locked price recap, slot selection, cancellation-policy agreement checkbox, card capture (Test adapter), converts lead → client+property+plan/job, issues portal magic link. Harvest the lead's token from psql (leads table) after submitting /book.
- /portal/access/:token → session → /portal (upcoming visits + named/photo cleaner + history with proof-of-work); /portal/visits/:id (reschedule/cancel gated by the cancellation policy — late-cancel fee shown BEFORE confirm; changes notify office/cleaner); /portal/invoices (pay via card on file, manage card, add tip preset/custom — tip must reach the cleaner's earnings on /field, verify as qa-cleaner). Harvest portal session tokens from psql (portal_sessions) or the acceptance flow.
- /reviews/:token — public review page (1-5 stars + text; rating <=3 offers private complaint routed to owner, NOT published); /reviews — owner-only inbox. Review requests: thank-you email on completion + request ~24h later (verify via psql notifications/reviews tables + any visible owner surface; time-travel by updating the job's updated_at via psql is sanctioned).
- Story specs and criteria: read each start_task prompt; BDD files under test/spex/<story>_*/ show exact expected behaviors/selectors.

Cross-cutting checks: cleaners/owners must NOT be able to see other accounts' portal data via token guessing (401/redirect on bad tokens); office pages still owner-only; the public pages must render styled (assets 200) and be mobile-viewport friendly (spot-check one page at 390x844).

Final response: one line per story with verdict + issue ids. Under 120 words.
</teammate-message>

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# QA Story 848: Get an instant quote from the public website

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want a public instant-quote form (bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage, frequency, add-ons) that shows me a real price from the company's rate card before I hand over contact details, so that I can decide in one sitting instead of waiting for a callback I may never answer. (Research: instant-quote booking forms are the residential standard and convert where request-a-quote friction loses time-pressured jobs — customer-side.md §1, §3)

## Acceptance criteria

- Building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info
- Building a quote by square footage instead of room counts
- Changing any input recomputes the total live
- Selecting bi-weekly frequency applies the recurring discount
- Selecting add-ons increases the running total
- Unsupported input combination shows a message instead of a wrong price
- Instant quote price matches the later acceptance total

Per-story QA testing brief. Written by the QA planner after reading the story's prompt file and the QA plan. Gives the tester exact instructions — tool, auth, seeds, what to test.

## Required Sections

### Tool

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: tool name (web, curl, or script path)

Content:
- Which tool to use for this story's testing
- `web` for LiveView pages, `curl` or script path for controller/API routes


### Auth

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands or instructions the tester copies verbatim

Content:
- Login URL, credentials, headers — whatever the tool needs
- Reference auth scripts from the QA plan if applicable
- Tester should not need to figure out auth on their own


### Seeds

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Exact commands to run

Content:
- Seed script references (`mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`)
- Any story-specific seed commands beyond the base seeds
- Entity IDs or values the tester will need


### What To Test

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Bullet list of specific test scenarios

Content:
- Specific URLs to visit
- Interactions to perform (click, fill form, submit)
- Expected outcomes (what the tester should see)
- Map to acceptance criteria from the story


### Result Path

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Single line: file path

Content:
- Where the tester writes the result document


## Optional Sections

### Setup Notes

Format:
- Use H2 heading
- Free-form paragraphs

Content:
- Additional context, prerequisites, known issues



## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

---

1	# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	## App Overview
4

# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

## Phase 2: Execute tests

There is no `result.md` artifact in this phase. Findings flow through
`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

### Tool rules — pick by Phoenix pipeline, not by guess

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

### Testing approach

- Capture a screenshot at each key state (initial load, after
  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for
  any finding that ships a screenshot.
- After scripted scenarios, explore freely: unexpected inputs, edge
  cases, empty states, anything that feels off.
- Reference existing scripts in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/` by path
  rather than inlining shell commands.

### Filing findings

The moment you observe something wrong — a broken UI, a 500, a missing
feature, an unexpected behavior — call `create_issue` and hold the
returned id. Don't accumulate findings in a notepad. Don't write them
into a markdown file. The DB issue is the canonical record.

- `title` — short, scannable.
- `severity` — critical / high / medium / low / info.
- `scope` — `app` for app-under-development bugs; `qa` for QA infrastructure
  problems; `docs` for docs gaps; (`framework` is a server-side concept and
  not selectable from the local list_issues filter, but `create_issue`
  itself supports it for harness issues).
- `story_id` — the story this finding relates to, when relevant.
- `description` — the reproduction, the expected vs actual, file paths,
  and any screenshot or evidence path.

If a finding is a duplicate of an existing issue (you'll see them in the
prompt's "Existing Issues" section), don't refile.

### Procedure

1. Read the brief at `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` for the
   complete plan.
2. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for auth strategy and seed commands.
3. Read `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling.md` and `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/`
   for tool usage patterns.
4. Run seed scripts to set up test data.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source to
   understand implementation details.
6. Execute each test scenario from the brief.
7. Capture screenshots at key states (save to the screenshots directory).
8. For every finding, call `create_issue` immediately and remember the id.
9. If you find a gap in the plan or the brief, fix it in-flight — update
   `plan.md` or `brief.md` rather than working around the gap.
10. Call `submit_qa_result` once at the end with `status`, the structured
    `scenarios` list, and the full `issue_ids` list. Then stop the session.

## What the evaluator does when you stop

The evaluator runs a thin check chain:

1. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` exists with required sections.
   (If missing, returns invalid pointing at `qa_setup`.)
2. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` exists and parses.
3. Checks whether a DB-backed pass attempt exists via
   `CodeMySpec.Qa.qa_complete?/2`. If yes, the requirement is satisfied
   and the session ends.
4. If no DB attempt exists but the brief is valid, feedback is returned
   demanding a `submit_qa_result` call. The requirement does NOT satisfy
   off a brief alone.

## The submit_qa_result contract

```
submit_qa_result(
  task_id: <task_id from start_task>,
  status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
  scenarios: [
    %{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."},
    ...
  ],
  issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue this run>]
)
```

Rules:

- `status: "pass"` with `issue_ids: []` is allowed — clean pass, nothing to
  file.
- `status: "partial"` or `"fail"` with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected** by
  the tool. File the findings first.
- Only `status: "pass"` satisfies the `qa_complete` requirement. Other
  statuses record an audit row but leave the requirement open.
- Resubmitting on the same `task_id` is allowed — each call creates a new
  attempt; the latest is canonical.

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
```

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

# Public routes
smoke "/"
smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

# Authenticated routes should redirect to login
smoke "/accounts" 302

exit $FAIL
```

- Accept 302 as valid for auth-protected routes when not logged in

- Use `mix phx.routes` output to build the route list

### Login page structure

The `/users/log-in` page renders **two separate forms** side by side:
- `#login_form_magic` — email-only form that sends a magic link
- `#login_form_password` — email + password form that submits via `POST /users/log-in`

The password form is often **below the viewport fold** because it comes after the magic link form. You must scroll it into view before interacting, or interaction tools will timeout waiting for the element to be actionable.

### Re-authentication mode

When a user has an existing session (e.g., session expired but cookie remains), Phoenix renders the login page in re-auth mode where the email field has a `readonly` attribute. Detect this and skip the email field:

```
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
```

If the result is `true`, skip the email fill step.

### Reference login sequence (MCP tools)

```

# 2. CRITICAL: scroll password form into view — it's below the magic link form
browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")

# 3. Check for re-auth mode (readonly email field)
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
# If false, fill email:
browser_fill(selector: "#login_form_password_email", text: "qa@example.com")

# 4. Fill password
browser_fill(selector: "#user_password", text: "hello world!")

# 5. Click "Log in and stay logged in"
browser_click(selector: "#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']")

# 6. Wait for page to load after redirect
browser_wait(selector: "body", timeout: 5000)
```

### Reference logout sequence (MCP tools)

Phoenix logout uses a `<a href="/users/log-out" data-method="delete">` link. Phoenix JS intercepts the click and issues a DELETE request. Just click the link:

```
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/")
browser_click(selector: "a[href='/users/log-out']")
```

### User switching

To test multi-user scenarios, log out first then log in as a different user using the login sequence above with different credentials.

`phx.gen.auth` requires email confirmation before password login works. Seeds must confirm users programmatically:

```elixir

# Confirm via magic link token (bypasses email)
{token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
Repo.insert!(user_token)
{:ok, {confirmed_user, _}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

# Set password after confirmation (magic link clears tokens)
{:ok, {final_user, _}} = Users.update_user_password(confirmed_user, %{password: password})
```

### Core workflow

Every browser automation follows this pattern:

1. **Launch**: `browser_launch` (once per session, if not already running)
2. **Navigate**: `browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000")`
3. **Map**: `browser_map` (get element refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
4. **Interact**: Use refs to click, fill, select — e.g. `browser_click(selector: "@e1")`
5. **Re-map**: After navigation or DOM changes, get fresh refs with `browser_map`

**Step 1: Log in once at the start of the QA session**
```
browser_launch(headless: true)
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/users/log-in")
browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")
browser_fill(selector: "#login_form_password_email", text: "qa@example.com")
browser_fill(selector: "#user_password", text: "hello world!")
browser_click(selector: "#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/dashboard")
```

`phx.gen.auth` generates predictable form IDs: `login_form_password` for password login, `login_form_magic` for passwordless/magic-link login, `registration_form` for registration.

**Step 2: Browse freely**
```
# Read page content as text
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/dashboard")
browser_get_text()

# Take a screenshot for evidence
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/settings")
browser_screenshot(filename: "settings.png")

# Get raw HTML when you need to inspect DOM structure
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items")
browser_get_html()
```

### Verifying page content

```
# Read all page text
browser_get_text()

# Read text within a specific element
browser_get_text(selector: "h1")
browser_get_text(selector: ".flash-message")

# Count elements
browser_count(selector: ".item")

# Check element state
browser_is_visible(selector: ".modal")
browser_is_enabled(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_get_value(selector: "input[name=email]")
browser_get_attribute(selector: "a", attribute: "href")

# Programmatic checks via JS
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('h1')?.textContent")
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelectorAll('.item').length")
```

### Interacting with LiveView pages

LiveView pages work like any other page with Vibium MCP. After interactions that trigger server-side changes, use explicit waits:

```

browser_wait_for_text(text: "deleted")

# Submit a LiveView form
browser_fill(selector: "#item_name", text: "Test Item")
browser_click(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")

# Trigger a phx-change event (e.g., select dropdown)
browser_select(selector: "select[name='filter']", value: "active")

# Wait for LiveView to reconnect after navigation
browser_wait(selector: "[data-phx-session]", state: "attached")
```

### Filling and submitting forms

Use `browser_map` to discover form fields, then `browser_fill` to set values:

```

browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items/new")
browser_map(selector: "form")
# Map output shows: @e1 [input] name="item[name]", @e2 [textarea] name="item[description]", @e3 [button] "Save"
browser_fill(selector: "@e1", text: "Test Item")
browser_fill(selector: "@e2", text: "Created by QA")
browser_click(selector: "@e3")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")
```

Use `browser_fill` to replace a field's value (clears first), `browser_type` to append to existing value.

### Semantic element discovery

Find elements without CSS selectors:
```
browser_find(text: "Sign In")           # by visible text
browser_find(label: "Email")            # by form label
browser_find(placeholder: "Search...")  # by placeholder
browser_find(testid: "submit-btn")      # by data-testid
browser_find(role: "button")            # by ARIA role
browser_find(alt: "Logo")              # by alt attribute
browser_click(selector: "@e1")          # click whatever was found
```

### Screenshots as evidence

Always take screenshots for QA evidence, especially for visual checks:
```
browser_screenshot(filename: "qa_dashboard.png")
browser_screenshot(filename: "annotated.png", annotate: true)
browser_screenshot(filename: "full.png", fullPage: true)
```

### Advanced interactions

```
# File upload
browser_upload(selector: "input[type=file]", files: ["./document.pdf"])

# Multi-tab workflows (OAuth redirects, popups)
browser_new_tab(url: "http://external-provider.com/authorize")
browser_click(selector: "#authorize-button")
browser_switch_tab(index: 0)

# Drag-and-drop
browser_drag(source: ".draggable", target: ".drop-target")

# Keyboard shortcuts
browser_keys(keys: "Control+a")
browser_press(key: "Enter", selector: "#search-input")

# Hover interactions
browser_hover(selector: ".menu-trigger")

# Viewport testing
browser_set_viewport(width: 375, height: 812)  # iPhone viewport
browser_screenshot(filename: "mobile.png")
```

### Key tools by category

| Category | MCP Tools |
|----------|-----------|
| Navigate | `browser_navigate`, `browser_back`, `browser_forward`, `browser_reload`, `browser_get_url`, `browser_get_title` |
| Discover | `browser_map`, `browser_diff_map`, `browser_find`, `browser_find_all`, `browser_count` |
| Read | `browser_get_text`, `browser_get_html`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_a11y_tree`, `browser_evaluate` |
| Interact | `browser_click`, `browser_dblclick`, `browser_fill`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_hover`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_keys`, `browser_select`, `browser_check`, `browser_uncheck` |
| Forms | `browser_fill` (clear+type), `browser_type` (append), `browser_select`, `browser_upload`, `browser_get_value` |
| State | `browser_is_visible`, `browser_is_enabled`, `browser_is_checked`, `browser_get_attribute`, `browser_get_value` |
| Wait | `browser_wait`, `browser_wait_for_url`, `browser_wait_for_text`, `browser_wait_for_load`, `browser_wait_for_fn` |
| Tabs | `browser_list_tabs`, `browser_new_tab`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_close_tab` |
| Auth | `browser_storage_state`, `browser_restore_storage`, `browser_get_cookies`, `browser_set_cookie`, `browser_delete_cookies` |
| Capture | `browser_screenshot` (`fullPage`, `annotate`), `browser_pdf` |
| Session | `browser_launch`, `browser_quit` |

### Troubleshooting

- **Stale refs?** Always re-map after navigation or DOM changes — refs are invalidated on page change
- **Element not actionable?** All interaction tools auto-wait, but use explicit `browser_wait` for dynamically loaded content
- **Need full tool reference?** See `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/vibium_reference.md`

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

```elixir
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")

    user
  user ->

    user
end

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---

account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

```
browser_click(selector: "button[type=submit]")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")

# Trigger a phx-change event (e.g., select dropdown)
browser_select(selector: "select[name='filter']", value: "active")

# Wait for LiveView to reconnect after navigation
browser_wait(selector: "[data-phx-session]", state: "attached")
```

### Filling and submitting forms

Use `browser_map` to discover form fields, then `browser_fill` to set values:

```
# Create a new item via form
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/items/new")
browser_map(selector: "form")
# Map output shows: @e1 [input] name="item[name]", @e2 [textarea] name="item[description]", @e3 [button] "Save"
browser_fill(selector: "@e1", text: "Test Item")
browser_fill(selector: "@e2", text: "Created by QA")
browser_click(selector: "@e3")
browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/items")
```

Use `browser_fill` to replace a field's value (clears first), `browser_type` to append to existing value.

### Semantic element discovery

Find elements without CSS selectors:
```
browser_find(text: "Sign In")           # by visible text
browser_find(label: "Email")            # by form label
browser_find(placeholder: "Search...")  # by placeholder
browser_find(testid: "submit-btn")      # by data-testid
browser_find(role: "button")            # by ARIA role
browser_find(alt: "Logo")              # by alt attribute
browser_click(selector: "@e1")          # click whatever was found
```

### Screenshots as evidence

Always take screenshots for QA evidence, especially for visual checks:
```
browser_screenshot(filename: "qa_dashboard.png")
browser_screenshot(filename: "annotated.png", annotate: true)
browser_screenshot(filename: "full.png", fullPage: true)
```

### Advanced interactions

```
# File upload
browser_upload(selector: "input[type=file]", files: ["./document.pdf"])

# Multi-tab workflows (OAuth redirects, popups)
browser_new_tab(url: "http://external-provider.com/authorize")
browser_click(selector: "#authorize-button")
browser_switch_tab(index: 0)

# Drag-and-drop
browser_drag(source: ".draggable", target: ".drop-target")

# Keyboard shortcuts
browser_keys(keys: "Control+a")
browser_press(key: "Enter", selector: "#search-input")

# Hover interactions
browser_hover(selector: ".menu-trigger")

# Viewport testing
browser_set_viewport(width: 375, height: 812)  # iPhone viewport
browser_screenshot(filename: "mobile.png")
```

### Key tools by category

| Category | MCP Tools |
|----------|-----------|
| Navigate | `browser_navigate`, `browser_back`, `browser_forward`, `browser_reload`, `browser_get_url`, `browser_get_title` |
| Discover | `browser_map`, `browser_diff_map`, `browser_find`, `browser_find_all`, `browser_count` |
| Read | `browser_get_text`, `browser_get_html`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_a11y_tree`, `browser_evaluate` |
| Interact | `browser_click`, `browser_dblclick`, `browser_fill`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_hover`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_keys`, `browser_select`, `browser_check`, `browser_uncheck` |
| Forms | `browser_fill` (clear+type), `browser_type` (append), `browser_select`, `browser_upload`, `browser_get_value` |
| State | `browser_is_visible`, `browser_is_enabled`, `browser_is_checked`, `browser_get_attribute`, `browser_get_value` |
| Wait | `browser_wait`, `browser_wait_for_url`, `browser_wait_for_text`, `browser_wait_for_load`, `browser_wait_for_fn` |
| Tabs | `browser_list_tabs`, `browser_new_tab`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_close_tab` |
| Auth | `browser_storage_state`, `browser_restore_storage`, `browser_get_cookies`, `browser_set_cookie`, `browser_delete_cookies` |
| Capture | `browser_screenshot` (`fullPage`, `annotate`), `browser_pdf` |
| Session | `browser_launch`, `browser_quit` |

### Troubleshooting

- **Stale refs?** Always re-map after navigation or DOM changes — refs are invalidated on page change
- **Element not actionable?** All interaction tools auto-wait, but use explicit `browser_wait` for dynamically loaded content
- **Need full tool reference?** See `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/vibium_reference.md`

The agent calls MCP tools directly for login/logout/QA setup. See the "Reference login sequence" and "Reference logout sequence" sections above for the tool call patterns.

For QA session setup:

2. Launch browser: `browser_launch(headless: true)`
3. Log in using the login sequence above
4. Browse and test

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7215Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7215 — Building a quote with room counts shows a price
  with no contact info: a real price is shown from selecting a
  service type and room counts alone, before any name, email, or
  phone is entered.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the public quote form prices a per-room home before contact info is given" do
    scenario "building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info" do
      given_ "a business with a per-room rate card and a visitor on the public quote page",
             context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the visitor selects a service type, bedroom count, and bathroom count without entering a name, email, or phone",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 2}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "a real price computed from the rate card is displayed immediately", context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$210.00")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7219Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7219 — Selecting add-ons increases the running total by
  the sum of each selected add-on's configured amount.
  """

            quote: %{add_ons: ["inside_fridge", "interior_windows"]}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the running total increases by the sum of both add-ons' configured amounts",

    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7220Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7220 — Unsupported input combination shows a message
  instead of a wrong price: when the rate card can't price a selected
  service type and size combination, the form withholds a price
  rather than showing $0 or a guess.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an unpriceable combination shows a clear message instead of a wrong price" do
    scenario "unsupported input combination shows a message instead of a wrong price" do
      given_ "a business's rate card has no configured price for a selected service type and size combination",
             context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000,
          per_sqft_rate_cents: nil
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the visitor selects that unsupported combination", context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 2000}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the form shows a clear \"can't price this yet, request a custom quote\" message instead of displaying $0 or a guessed price",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']")
        assert render(context.quote_live) =~ "can't price this yet"
        assert render(context.quote_live) =~ "request a custom quote"
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$0.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7221Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7221 — Instant quote price matches the later acceptance
  total: the number shown on the instant-quote calculator is exactly
  the number carried through to the accept-and-book step, with no
  added fees.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the instant quote total carries through unchanged to acceptance" do
    scenario "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" do
      given_ "a visitor sees an instant quote total of $195 in integer cents", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 6000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3750
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 2, bathroom_count: 2}
        )
        |> render_change()

        assert has_element?(quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$195.00")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "they proceed to the accept-and-book step without changing any selections", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='lead-contact-form']",
          lead: %{name: "Dana Prescott", email: "dana@example.com", phone: "555-0142"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        path = assert_patch(context.quote_live)
        {:ok, accept_live, html} = live(context.conn, path)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{accept_live: accept_live, html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the total shown at acceptance is exactly $195 with no added fees", context do
        assert context.html =~ "$195.00"
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='added-fee']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

# QA seed script — idempotent. Run with: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates two confirmed users with passwords (an owner and a cleaner) and
# one account (the cleaning company) owned by the owner. Prints credentials.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

ensure_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})

      # Confirm via the magic-link flow (same path a real user takes).
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

owner = ensure_user.("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")
cleaner = ensure_user.("qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test")

owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

account =
  case Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope) do
    [account | _] ->
      account

    [] ->
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co"})
      account
  end

# The cleaner must be an account member: office surfaces are gated on
# owner/admin role, and field surfaces scope by the active account.
case Accounts.get_user_role(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id) do
  nil -> {:ok, _} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, cleaner.id, account.id, :member)
  _role -> :ok
end

IO.puts("""

QA seed complete.

  Owner:   qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Cleaner: qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Account: #{account.name} (id: #{account.id})

  Log in at: http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in
""")

# Qa Story Brief

## Tool

web

## Auth

None required — `/book` is a public, unauthenticated route. No login needed.

## Seeds

Base seeds already applied: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (owner qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / cleaner qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / account "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co", id `b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473`).

`Booking.public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account (see moduledoc in `lib/cleaner_crm/booking.ex`). Only one account exists in this DB, so `/book` prices against QA Sparkle Cleaning Co's rate card.

There is no owner-facing UI yet for the `RateCard` used by `/book` (the existing `/quotes` surface is a different model — one-off custom quotes, `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Quote` — not the rate card). The rate card was configured directly via psql for this QA pass:

```
per_room_bedroom_rate_cents = 5000   ($50/bedroom)
per_room_bathroom_rate_cents = 3000  ($30/bathroom)
per_sqft_rate_cents = 20             ($0.20/sqft)
hourly_rate_cents = NULL             (unconfigured — used to test the "unsupported" criterion)
weekly_discount_percent = 15
biweekly_discount_percent = 10
monthly_discount_percent = 5
add_on_rates_cents = {"inside_fridge": 1500, "interior_windows": 2000}
```

Verify with: `psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select * from rate_cards;"`

## What To Test

- Navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:4100/book`. Confirm page renders styled (trust badges, form) with no contact fields visible yet, and no price shown before any input (AC: room-count pricing needs no contact info).
- Select pricing model "Per room", bedroom count 3, bathroom count 2. Expect live total `$210.00` ((3*50)+(2*30)=150+60=210) with no name/email/phone required to see it. (AC1: criterion 7215)
- Switch pricing model to "Per square foot", enter square feet 2000. Expect total `$400.00` (2000*0.20). (AC2: criterion 7216)
- Back on per-room, set bedroom count 2 / bathroom 0 → expect `$100.00`; change bedroom count to 3 → expect total updates live to `$150.00` with no page reload (check URL doesn't change, no full navigation). (AC3: criterion 7217)
- With bedroom 2 / bathroom 0 / frequency "One-time" → `$100.00`. Switch frequency to "Bi-weekly" → expect `$90.00` (10% off) and a discount note referencing "bi-weekly discount". (AC4: criterion 7218)
- With bedroom 2 / bathroom 0 (base `$100.00`), check "Inside fridge" and "Interior windows" add-ons → expect total `$135.00` (100+15+20). (AC5: criterion 7219)
- Select pricing model "Hourly" and enter an hours value → expect the `[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']` element with text containing "can't price this yet" and "request a custom quote" — NOT a `$0.00` total. (AC6: criterion 7220)
- With bedroom 2 / bathroom 2 rates (6000/3750 cents if re-seeded per spex, or use current rate card: pick any combo and note the exact total shown, e.g. $210.00 for bedroom 3/bathroom 2), fill the lead contact form (name/email/phone) and submit. Confirm it patches to `/book/accept/:token` and the SAME total is shown with no added fees. (AC7: criterion 7221)
- Explore: try 0/negative/blank bedroom counts, huge square footage, rapid input changes, and submitting the contact form with invalid email — note any crashes, wrong prices, or unhandled states.
- Mobile check: set viewport to 390x844 and screenshot `/book` to confirm it's usable at mobile width.
- Confirm static assets load (200) — no broken CSS/JS on `/book`.

## Result Path

Findings are filed via `create_issue` as discovered; final record is the `submit_qa_result` DB attempt (task id `28f51d76-22c3-4250-82e5-017e52352c3a`). Screenshots: `.code_my_spec/qa/848/screenshots/`.

input.title: /book header nav overflows viewport on mobile (390px), causing horizontal scroll
input.description:
On the public instant-quote page (/book) at a 390x844 mobile viewport, the shared root layout header's nav (Register/Log in top row, then logo + Website/GitHub/theme-toggle/Get Started second row) does not wrap or collapse. `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` measures 521px against a `clientWidth` of 390px — a 131px horizontal overflow — forcing the whole page to horizontal-scroll on mobile.

Confirmed via browser_evaluate on the live page:
```
scrollWidth: 521, clientWidth: 390
headerRect: {x:0, y:49, width:390, height:64}
innerUlRect (Website/GitHub/theme-toggle/Get Started): {x:64, width:456.97, right:521}
```

Screenshot: ~/Pictures/Vibium/07_mobile_390x844.png and 08_mobile_header_check.png (also visually shows the logo's "v1.8.9" badge crowding the "Website" link).

This is the shared `CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts.app` header (lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex), so it affects every page using this layout, but it's especially relevant for /book since that's the new public, mobile-first conversion funnel entry point (story 848) — a horizontally-scrolling header undermines the "one sitting" instant-quote experience on phones, the primary device for this flow.

Expected: header nav collapses into a hamburger/menu or wraps at narrow widths so the page has no horizontal overflow.
Actual: nav overflows the viewport by 131px, causing horizontal scroll.

content.text:
# QA Story 849: Accept a quote and book online with card on file

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want to accept my quote online — pick a slot, agree to the cancellation policy, and put a card on file — so that booking is done in minutes and the price I saw is the price I'm charged. (Research: Jobber captures cards at quote acceptance; capturing policy agreement at booking is best practice; bait-and-switch pricing is a top category complaint — customer-side.md §1, §2)

## Acceptance criteria

- Client selects an open slot and proceeds to review
- Selected slot becomes unavailable before confirmation
- Client views and agrees to the cancellation policy before confirming
- Booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement
- Client enters a valid card and the booking confirms
- Payment gateway declines the card
- Card is authorized for the exact quoted amount
- Confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want to accept my quote online — pick a slot, agree to the cancellation policy, and put a card on file — so that booking is done in minutes and the price I saw is the price I'm charged. (Research: Jobber captures cards at quote acceptance; capturing policy agreement at booking is best practice; bait-and-switch pricing is a top category complaint — customer-side.md §1, §2)

- Client selects an open slot and proceeds to review
- Selected slot becomes unavailable before confirmation
- Client views and agrees to the cancellation policy before confirming
- Booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement
- Client enters a valid card and the booking confirms
- Payment gateway declines the card
- Card is authorized for the exact quoted amount
- Confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7228Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7228 — Client selects an open slot and proceeds to
  review: picking an available date and time advances the booking
  flow to cancellation policy and payment.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "selecting an open slot advances to cancellation policy and payment" do
    scenario "client selects an open slot and proceeds to review" do
      given_ "a client has an accepted instant quote and the business has open slots", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead =
          Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{
            total_cents: 19_500,
            client_name: "Dana Prescott",
            client_email: "dana@example.com"
          })

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client selects an available date and time", context do
        html =
          context.accept_live
          |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
            booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
          )
          |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the booking flow proceeds to cancellation policy and payment", context do
        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")
        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='policy-agreement-checkbox']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7230Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7230 — Selected slot becomes unavailable before
  confirmation: if another booking claims the same slot before this
  client confirms, the confirmation is blocked and no charge is made.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a slot claimed by another booking blocks confirmation" do
    scenario "selected slot becomes unavailable before confirmation" do
      given_ "a client has selected a time slot but another booking claims it first", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        scheduled_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: scheduled_date, start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        other_client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Other Client"})

        Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, other_client, %{
          scheduled_date: scheduled_date,
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client attempts to confirm the booking", context do
        html =
          context.accept_live
          |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
            booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
          )
          |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the booking is blocked with a message to pick another slot and no charge is made",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='slot-unavailable-error']")
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7231Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7231 — Client views and agrees to the cancellation policy
  before confirming: checking the agreement (24-hour notice and fee)
  lets the client proceed to payment.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "agreeing to the cancellation policy allows proceeding to payment" do
    scenario "client views and agrees to the cancellation policy before confirming" do
      given_ "the client has selected a slot and reached the confirmation step", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        assert render(accept_live) =~ "24-hour"

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the cancellation policy (24-hour notice and fee) is displayed and the client checks agreement",
            context do
        html =
          context.accept_live
          |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
            booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
          )
          |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the client is allowed to proceed to payment", context do
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='policy-required-error']")
        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7232Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7232 — Booking is blocked without cancellation policy
  agreement: trying to confirm without checking agreement leaves the
  booking unconfirmed and prompts the client to agree first.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "confirming without agreeing to the cancellation policy is blocked" do
    scenario "booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement" do
      given_ "the client has selected a slot and reached the confirmation step", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client tries to confirm without checking the cancellation policy agreement",
            context do
        html =
          context.accept_live
          |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
            booking: %{policy_agreed: "false", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
          )
          |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the booking is not confirmed and the client is prompted to agree first", context do
        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='policy-required-error']")
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7233Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7233 — Client enters a valid card and the booking
  confirms: once the payment gateway accepts the card, it is stored
  on file and the booking is confirmed.

  As with story 836's card charges, the gateway's acceptance is only
  final once the provider confirms it via `POST /webhooks/stripe`
  (see `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`) — submitting the card
  moves the booking to a pending-payment state; this spec's subject
  is the transition that follows the provider's confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the payment gateway accepting the card confirms the booking" do
    scenario "client enters a valid card and the booking confirms" do
      given_ "the client has agreed to the cancellation policy", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client enters a valid card and the payment gateway accepts it", context do
        context.accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_succeeded",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(context.lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the card is stored on file and the booking is confirmed", context do
        {:ok, accept_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7234Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7234 — Payment gateway declines the card: the booking is
  not confirmed and the client is prompted to retry with a different
  card.

  Mirrors story 836's decline handling: the provider's decline
  arrives via `POST /webhooks/stripe` (`payment_intent.payment_failed`),
  never as a synchronous response to submitting the card.
  """
