defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
  @moduledoc """
  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.

  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).

  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
  receive from a plug.

  ## Single-tenant storefront (known MVP limitation)

  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
  `public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account
  rather than *the right* one, matching the single-account assumption
  every story-848 spec drives (each spec's own account is the newest
  one the moment it hits `/book`, so this holds even alongside stray
  older rows). A multi-tenant deployment needs its own story to give
  each business a distinct public booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`)
  before this holds up outside a single-account deployment or test.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
  # builder default order of magnitude (see
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
  @default_occurrence_count 12
  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60

  ## Public storefront

  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}

  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)

  defp resolve_public_account_id do
    Account
    |> order_by(desc: :inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([a], a.id)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Instant quote (calculator)

  @doc """
  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
  `quote_summary/2`).
  """
  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

  @doc """
  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
  once contact info makes it one.
  """
  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  ## Acceptance: slot selection

  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead.
  Nothing reaches the database here — `confirm_booking/2` is the only
  place a slot gets written, so availability is always checked again
  right before a card is ever charged, no matter how long a client
  lingers on the cancellation-policy step.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment

  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false

  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
    Scheduling.slot_available?(
      scope_for(lead),
      lead.scheduled_date,
      lead.start_time,
      lead.end_time
    )
  end

  @doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, or the slot's been claimed by
  another booking since it was selected — otherwise submits the card
  and moves the lead to `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
  """
  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
        {:error, :policy_required}

      not slot_available?(lead) ->
        {:error, :slot_unavailable}

      true ->
        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      lead
      |> Lead.changeset(%{
        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        status: :payment_pending,
        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
      })
      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
      |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
  event isn't one of its own invoices.
  """
  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      convert_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      decline_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:error, :lead_not_found}

  defp find_lead_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"lead_id" => lead_id}} when is_binary(lead_id) -> fetch_lead(lead_id)
      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) -> fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id)
      _ -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead(lead_id) do
    case Repo.get(Lead, lead_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Lead, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp decline_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    lead |> Lead.changeset(%{status: :payment_declined}) |> Repo.update()
  end

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment

  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false

  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
    Scheduling.slot_available?(
      scope_for(lead),
      lead.scheduled_date,
      lead.start_time,
      lead.end_time
    )
  end

  @doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, or the slot's been claimed by
  another booking since it was selected — otherwise submits the card
  and moves the lead to `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
  """
  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
        {:error, :policy_required}

      not slot_available?(lead) ->
        {:error, :slot_unavailable}

      true ->
        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      lead
      |> Lead.changeset(%{
        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        status: :payment_pending,
        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
      })
      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
      |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
  event isn't one of its own invoices.
  """
  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      convert_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      decline_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:error, :lead_not_found}

  defp find_lead_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"lead_id" => lead_id}} when is_binary(lead_id) -> fetch_lead(lead_id)
      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) -> fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id)
      _ -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead(lead_id) do
    case Repo.get(Lead, lead_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Lead, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp decline_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    lead |> Lead.changeset(%{status: :payment_declined}) |> Repo.update()
  end

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

input.content:
# Qa Story Brief

## Tool

web (browser for `/book/accept/:token` and `/schedule`); curl for `POST /webhooks/stripe` (unauthenticated `:webhook` pipeline — confirms/declines only arrive this way, never synchronously from the confirmation form per criteria 7233/7234's own spex).

## Auth

None needed to create leads or view `/book/accept/:token` (public token-link route, no login).

For the "confirmed booking appears for the business" check (criterion 7236), log in as the owner via the browser: navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in`, scroll `#login_form_password` into view, fill `input[name="user[email]"]` = `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test`, `input[name="user[password]"]` = `qa password 1234`, click the password form's submit button, then visit `/schedule`.

## Seeds

Base seeds already applied (`mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`) — account "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co" (`b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473`), owner/cleaner confirmed users.

Each test scenario needs its OWN fresh lead (status transitions are one-way). Create one per scenario via the browser at `/book` (per-room, e.g. 2 bed/1 bath → $130.00) → fill the lead contact form → capture the acceptance token from the redirect URL `/book/accept/:token`, OR harvest directly:

```
psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, acceptance_token, status, total_cents, client_name from leads order by inserted_at desc limit 5;"
```

For the slot-unavailable scenario (criterion 7230), pre-seed a competing job at the exact date/time you're about to select in the browser (10 days out, 09:00–11:00):

```
psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "insert into jobs (id, account_id, scheduled_date, start_time, end_time, status, inserted_at, updated_at) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473', current_date + 10, '09:00', '11:00', 'scheduled', now(), now());"
```

## What To Test

- **Slot selection (7228):** create a lead, visit `/book/accept/:token`. Fill `[data-test='slot-form']` with a date 10 days out and start time 09:00, submit. Expect it advances to show `[data-test='confirmation-form']` and `[data-test='policy-agreement-checkbox']`.
- **Slot becomes unavailable (7230):** on a NEW lead, pre-insert a competing job at the same date/time (see Seeds), select that slot, then submit the confirmation form with the policy checkbox checked. Expect `[data-test='slot-unavailable-error']`, no `[data-test='payment-pending']`, no `[data-test='booking-confirmed']`, and verify via psql that the lead's `stripe_payment_intent_id` is still null (no charge attempted).

Expect `[data-test='policy-required-error']`, no payment-pending/confirmed. Then check the box and resubmit — expect it proceeds to `[data-test='payment-pending']` (mirrors the two criteria on one lead, checking the negative first).

content.text: This confirms a genuine bug: a fully converted booking with a "scheduled" job dated 2020-01-01 was created, with payment processed and no validation blocking it anywhere in the flow. Filing this issue.

input.title: Booking acceptance accepts and confirms a past date with no validation
input.description:
On `/book/accept/:token`, the slot-selection step (`[data-test='slot-form']`) accepts any date, including dates far in the past, with no validation error. Submitted `scheduled_date=2020-01-01` (today is 2026-07-08) and the flow proceeded normally through cancellation-policy agreement, payment (via the Stripe Test adapter), and full webhook confirmation.

Root cause: `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_changeset/2` (lib/cleaner_crm/booking/lead.ex:156-160) only does `cast` + `validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time])` — no `validate_date` / future-date check. Nothing downstream (`Booking.select_slot/2`, `Booking.confirm_booking/2`, `Booking.slot_available?/1`) checks the date is not in the past either — `slot_available?` only checks for overlapping jobs on that date, not whether the date has already passed.

Reproduced end-to-end: after completing the full flow with a `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook, the lead converted (`status='converted'`) and a real job was created with `scheduled_date = 2020-01-01`, `status = 'scheduled'` (verified via psql: `select l.status, l.scheduled_date, j.scheduled_date, j.status from leads l join jobs j on j.id=l.job_id where l.id='02cde8a4-0a28-46e3-b082-0956ac3a7dac'`).

Impact: a client can "confirm and pay" for a visit dated in the past, producing a permanently-unfulfillable "scheduled" job on the business's board and a card charge for a service that can never be delivered as booked, with no error shown to the client at any step.

Expected: the slot-form (client-side and/or server-side) should reject a `scheduled_date` that isn't in the future (or at minimum not in the past), before advancing past slot selection.

# QA Story 850: See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want a portal showing my upcoming visits with the named, photo-identified cleaner assigned, plus my service history with checklist results and before/after photos, so that I know who is entering my home and can see exactly what I paid for. (Research: trust is the #1 gate — 73% of bad experiences trace to trust; Jobber's Client Hub shows assigned-team photos for this reason — customer-side.md §1, §2)

## Acceptance criteria

- Client opens the portal via a valid magic link
- Expired or invalid magic link denies access
- Upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name and photo
- Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees
- Unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder
- Completed visit in history shows checklist and before/after photos
- Portal proof-of-work matches the invoice's evidence

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7251Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7251 — Client opens the portal via a valid magic link: the
  portal opens showing upcoming visits and service history, with no
  password required.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a valid magic-link token opens the client's portal" do
    scenario "client opens the portal via a valid magic link" do
      given_ "a client has been sent a magic-link token for their portal", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        session = Fixtures.portal_magic_link_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, session: session})}
      end

      when_ "the client follows the link", context do
        access_conn = get(context.conn, ~p"/portal/access/#{context.session.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :access_conn, access_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the portal opens showing their upcoming visits and service history without requiring a password",
            context do
        assert redirected_to(context.access_conn) == ~p"/portal"

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = context.access_conn |> recycle() |> live(~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='service-history']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7252Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7252 — Expired or invalid magic link denies access:
  access is denied and the client is offered a way to request a
  fresh link.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an expired magic-link token denies portal access" do
    scenario "expired or invalid magic link denies access" do
      given_ "a client's magic-link token has expired", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

        session =
          Fixtures.portal_magic_link_fixture(client, %{
            expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, session: session})}
      end

      when_ "the client follows the link", context do
        access_conn = get(context.conn, ~p"/portal/access/#{context.session.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :access_conn, access_conn)}
      end

      then_ "access to the portal is denied and the client is offered a way to request a fresh link",
            context do
        html = Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.access_conn, 200)
        assert html =~ ~r/expired|invalid/i
        assert html =~ ~r/request a new link|request a fresh link/i

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7253Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7253 — Upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name
  and photo alongside the date/time.

  The magic-link exchange itself is covered end-to-end by this
  story's own criterion 7251 spec, so the portal session is seeded
  directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.portal_session_fixture/1`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an upcoming visit shows its assigned cleaner's name and photo" do
    scenario "upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name and photo" do
      given_ "a client has an upcoming visit with a cleaner assigned", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, client, %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, client: client, job: job, conn: conn})}
      end

      when_ "the client views the portal", context do
        {:ok, portal_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/portal")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{portal_live: portal_live, html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the visit shows the date/time along with the cleaner's name and photo", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}']",
                 context.cleaner.name
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}'] [data-test='assigned-cleaner-photo']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7254Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7254 — Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client
  sees: the next time the portal is viewed, it shows the newly
  assigned cleaner.

  Reassignment is driven through the real dispatch board
  (`ScheduleLive.Board`, covered end-to-end by story 834's own
  reassignment specs), not seeded directly, since the board's
  cleaner-select is the actual mechanism that changes a job's
  assignment.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "reassigning a visit's cleaner is reflected the next time the portal is viewed" do
    scenario "reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees" do
      given_ "a client's upcoming visit currently shows Cleaner A", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner_a = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, client, %{cleaner_id: cleaner_a.id})
        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn, ~p"/portal")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}']", cleaner_a.name)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           scope: scope,
           account: account,
           cleaner_a: cleaner_a,
           client: client,
           job: job,
           portal_conn: portal_conn,
           owner_conn: owner_conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "the business reassigns the visit to Cleaner B", context do
        cleaner_b = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{name: "Sam Okafor"})

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(cleaner_b.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_b, cleaner_b)}
      end

      then_ "the client's portal shows Cleaner B's name and photo the next time it is viewed",
            context do
        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController do
  @moduledoc """
  The magic-link entry point into the client portal: `GET
  /portal/access/:token` exchanges a token (mailed to the client, or
  handed out at booking) for a portal session — no password
  required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Portal`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def access(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Portal.access_portal(token) do
      {:ok, client_id} ->
        conn
        |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client_id)
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/portal")

      {:error, :invalid} ->
        render(conn, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth do
  @moduledoc """
  Gates the client portal's LiveViews behind a magic-link session —
  no user login. Reads the client id `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController`
  wrote to the session's `:portal_client_id` key after a valid
  `/portal/access/:token` exchange, mirroring how
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth` reads `:user_token` for staff auth.

  ## Usage

      live_session :portal,
        on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
        live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def on_mount(:require_client, _params, session, socket) do
    case session["portal_client_id"] do
      nil ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "Please use your portal link to sign in.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/")

        {:halt, socket}

      client_id ->
        {:cont,
         Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :client, fn -> Portal.get_client!(client_id) end)}
    end
  end
end

  one that's expired — a client offered the same "your link is

    case Repo.get_by(PortalSession, token_hash: PortalSession.hash_token(token)) do
      nil -> {:error, :invalid}
      %PortalSession{} = session -> exchange(session)
    end

  defp exchange(%PortalSession{} = session) do
    if PortalSession.expired?(session) do
      {:error, :invalid}
    else
      {:ok, _touched} = session |> PortalSession.touch_changeset() |> Repo.update()
      {:ok, session.client_id}
    end
  end

  @doc "Loads a client by id — the portal session carries only the id, never the whole struct."
  def get_client!(client_id), do: Repo.get!(Client, client_id)

    |> account_scope()

    |> Enum.filter(&(Date.compare(&1.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :lt))
    |> Enum.sort_by(&{&1.scheduled_date, &1.start_time})

  checklist and before/after photos are read separately via
  `visit_checklist/1`.

  def list_visit_history(%Client{} = client) do
    client
    |> account_scope()
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.client_id == client.id and &1.status == :completed))
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.scheduled_date, {:desc, Date})

  alone isn't enough, since other clients on the same account must
  never reach each other's visits by guessing an id.

  @doc """

        "date" => date_input,
        "start_time" => start_time_input

    with :ok <- ensure_modifiable(job),
         {:ok, date} <- parse_date(date_input),
         {:ok, start_time} <- parse_time(start_time_input),

           Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{
             scheduled_date: date,
             start_time: start_time,
             end_time: shift_end_time(job, start_time)
           }) do
      notify_schedule_change(
        scope,
        updated,

    end

  the account's same-day fee if the visit is scheduled for today, its
  late fee if cancelling inside the notice window, otherwise zero.
  """

  the updated visit — computed against the moment cancellation was
  requested, not looked up again afterward — and notifies the

      when not is_nil(account_id) do

    |> get_cancellation_policy()
    |> CancellationPolicy.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  ## Invoices and payment

  @doc "Every invoice for `client`'s own jobs, most recent first."
  def list_invoices(%Client{} = client) do
    Invoice
    |> join(:inner, [i], j in Job, on: j.id == i.job_id)

  @doc """
  Pays an invoice from the portal: submits the charge (per the
  payments-stripe ADR, this only moves the invoice to
  `:charge_pending` — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven), then
  optionally saves the card on file and records a tip against the
  visit's assigned cleaner.

  `attrs` (string-keyed, straight off the payment form): `"card_token"`
  (required), `"save_card"` (`"true"`/`"on"` to save), `"tip_cents"`
  (blank or omitted to skip the tip).
  """
  def pay_invoice(%Client{} = client, %Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    with {:ok, updated_invoice} <- Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, Map.get(attrs, "card_token")) do
      maybe_save_card(client, attrs)
      maybe_record_tip(updated_invoice, attrs)
      {:ok, updated_invoice}
    end
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(%Client{} = client, %{"save_card" => save_card})
       when save_card in ["true", "on"] do
    Clients.update_client(system_scope(client.account_id), client, %{card_on_file: true})
  end

  defp maybe_save_card(_client, _attrs), do: :ok

  defp maybe_record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, attrs) do
    case parse_tip_cents(Map.get(attrs, "tip_cents")) do
      cents when is_integer(cents) and cents > 0 -> record_tip(invoice, cents)
      _no_tip -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp record_tip(%Invoice{} = invoice, cents) do
    %Tip{
      account_id: invoice.account_id,
      invoice_id: invoice.id,
      cleaner_id: invoice.job.cleaner_id
    }
    |> Tip.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: cents,
      stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Cents a cleaner has been tipped through the portal within `period`
  (a `{start_date, end_date}` tuple, matching
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.current_pay_period/1`'s own shape) — read
  by `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.EarningsComponent` to fold tips into a
  cleaner's pay-period total alongside their time-tracked earnings.
  """
  def tip_cents_for_cleaner(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        cleaner_id,
        {start_date, end_date}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    Tip
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        t.inserted_at >= ^start_at and t.inserted_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> select([t], sum(t.amount_cents))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> Kernel.||(0)
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  defp account_scope(%Client{account_id: account_id}), do: system_scope(account_id)

  defp system_scope(account_id), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{status: status}) when status in [:completed, :cancelled],
    do: {:error, :not_modifiable}

  defp ensure_modifiable(%Job{}), do: :ok

  defp parse_date(%Date{} = date), do: {:ok, date}
  defp parse_date(string) when is_binary(string), do: Date.from_iso8601(string)

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _other -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when value in [nil, ""], do: nil

  defp parse_tip_cents(value) when is_binary(value) do
    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {cents, _rest} -> cents
      :error -> nil
    end
  end

  # Moves `start_time` in by the same amount the visit already runs,
  # clamping to end-of-day rather than wrapping past midnight into an
  # earlier clock time — mirrors
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`' own `default_end_time/1` safeguard.
  defp shift_end_time(%Job{} = job, %Time{} = start_time) do
    {start_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.start_time)
    {end_seconds, _} = Time.to_seconds_after_midnight(job.end_time)
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, end_seconds - start_seconds, :second)

    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  defp hours_until_visit(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}) do
    visit_at = DateTime.new!(date, time, "Etc/UTC")
    DateTime.diff(visit_at, DateTime.utc_now(), :hour)
  end

  defp notify_schedule_change(_scope, %Job{cleaner_id: nil}, _summary), do: :ok

  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, %Job{} = job, summary) do
    Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{
      cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :schedule_change,
      channel: :push,
      status: :pending,
      change_summary: summary,
      pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
      token: "portal_schedule_change_#{job.id}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
    })
  end

  defp schedule_label(%Job{} = job),
    do:
      "#{job.scheduled_date} #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)}-#{format_time_12h(job.end_time)}"

  defp format_time_12h(%Time{} = time) do
    {hour, period} = to_12_hour(time.hour)
    minute = time.minute |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")
    "#{hour}:#{minute} #{period}"
  end

  defp to_12_hour(0), do: {12, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour) when hour < 12, do: {hour, "AM"}
  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Portal.PortalSession do
  @moduledoc """
  A magic-link access token that lets a client into their portal with
  no password account.

  The plaintext token is only ever held in memory — in the `:token`
  virtual field, right after `build_changeset/2` creates it — to be
  mailed or handed to the client; only its SHA-256 hash is persisted.
  This mirrors `CleanerCrm.Users.UserToken`'s own magic-link scheme, so
  read access to the database alone can never reconstruct a working
  token.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @hash_algorithm :sha256
  @rand_size 32
  @default_validity_in_days 7

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          token: String.t() | nil,
          token_hash: binary() | nil,
          expires_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          last_used_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "portal_sessions" do
    field :token, :string, virtual: true
    field :token_hash, :binary
    field :expires_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :last_used_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a fresh session for `client`: a random plaintext token (held
  only in the returned changeset's `:token` virtual field, for the
  caller to mail or hand back) and its hash, expiring
  #{@default_validity_in_days} days out unless `attrs` gives its own
  `:expires_at`.
  """
  def build_changeset(%{id: client_id, account_id: account_id}, attrs) do
    token = generate_token()

    %__MODULE__{account_id: account_id, client_id: client_id}
    |> cast(attrs, [:expires_at, :last_used_at])
    |> put_change(:token, token)
    |> put_change(:token_hash, hash_token(token))
    |> put_default_expiry()
    |> validate_required([:account_id, :client_id, :token_hash, :expires_at])
  end

  @doc "Marks the session used just now."
  def touch_changeset(%__MODULE__{} = session) do
    change(session, last_used_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  @doc "Hashes a plaintext token the same way `build_changeset/2` does, for lookup by token."
  def hash_token(token) when is_binary(token), do: :crypto.hash(@hash_algorithm, token)

  @doc "True once `expires_at` has passed."
  def expired?(%__MODULE__{expires_at: expires_at}),
    do: DateTime.compare(expires_at, DateTime.utc_now()) == :lt

  defp put_default_expiry(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :expires_at) do
      nil ->
        put_change(
          changeset,
          :expires_at,
          DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), @default_validity_in_days, :day)
        )

      _expires_at ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_token,
    do: @rand_size |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
end

content.text: The access control correctly prevented cross-client data leakage — no data leaked, an exception fired — but the failure surfaces as a raw stack-trace debug page rather than a clean "not found." Since this QA environment runs in dev config (`debug_errors: true`), this wouldn't leak in a real production build, but it's still worth flagging as a UX/robustness gap.

input.title: Cross-client portal visit access raises unhandled exception instead of a clean not-found page
input.description:
Visiting `/portal/visits/:job_id` with a job id that belongs to a DIFFERENT client than the current portal session correctly denies access (no cross-client data is ever rendered) — `CleanerCrm.Portal.get_visit!/2` (lib/cleaner_crm/portal.ex:110-117) deliberately raises `Ecto.NoResultsError` when `job.client_id != client.id`. Verified: no other client's visit details leaked.

However, nothing in `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.Visit` (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/portal_live/visit.ex:101) rescues or maps that exception to a friendly page. In this QA environment (`config/dev.exs` sets `debug_errors: true`), the raised exception renders as a full Phoenix/Plug.Debugger stack-trace page, including internal file paths, the request's session, and params. Reproduced: GET `/portal/visits/5f317af1-7bda-4675-9c00-ab8840913f43` while authenticated as a different client's portal session.

Note: in a real production build (`debug_errors` unset/false), Phoenix/phoenix_ecto's built-in handling maps `Ecto.NoResultsError` to a generic 404 automatically, so this wouldn't leak internals there -- this is not a data-exposure vulnerability. But the client-facing experience for this case (mistyped/stale visit link, or a link to a visit that's since been reassigned/removed) is a bare unbranded error page in every environment, not the friendly "we couldn't find that" messaging this app already uses elsewhere (e.g. the booking acceptance page's `[data-test='not_found']`-style copy for bad tokens). Suggest catching this case in `PortalLive.Visit.mount/3` and rendering the same kind of friendly not-found state used by the booking flow.

input.title: Proof-of-work photos for job e604cc04 (QA Card Client 836) reference nonexistent files — broken images
input.description: While verifying story 850 criteria 7256/7257 (portal + invoice proof-of-work photos), the `` elements render correctly with the right `data-test` attributes ([data-test='before-photo']/[data-test='after-photo']/[data-test='proof-of-work-photo']) and match exactly between `/portal` and `/invoices/:id` (same `src` values), but the images themselves are broken (browser shows the broken-image icon). Root cause is stale/synthetic seed data, not the rendering code: the three `photos` rows attached to checklist `773de3d5-200b-4dc3-b409-629bd609c741` (job `e604cc04-c345-4638-9476-cfdbab3c33a6`, client "QA Card Client 836", likely seeded during an earlier story-836 QA session) have `storage_key` values (`/uploads/4130-before1.png`, `/uploads/4226-after1.png`, `/uploads/4322-retry_before.png`) that don't correspond to any file in `priv/static/uploads/` (confirmed via `ls` + direct `curl` -> 404 for all three). Other photo rows in the same directory (412 real files, e.g. `4226-after_kitchen.jpg`) show the real upload naming convention is `-.`, so these three look like hand-typed placeholder strings rather than real uploads. This isn't an app code bug -- `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.Home`'s `` and the invoice's proof-of-work rendering are both correct, and the criteria's literal DOM assertions (element presence, same src between portal/invoice) pass. Filing as `qa` scope so the stale seed rows get cleaned up or repointed at real files, since anyone spot-checking this specific job in the running QA environment sees broken images instead of real proof-of-work photos.

# QA Story 851: Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want to reschedule or cancel an upcoming visit from the portal within the company's stated notice policy (with any late fee shown before I confirm), so that I stay in control without phone tag and the company isn't blindsided. (Research: self-service reschedule/cancel within a 24–48h policy is the expectation; captured policy agreement prevents disputes — customer-side.md §1)

## Acceptance criteria

- Client reschedules a visit from the portal
- Late cancellation shows fee before confirming
- On-time cancellation has no fee
- Reschedule notifies office and cleaner
- Reschedule preserves price and scope
- Cannot modify a completed visit
- Same-day cancellation charges the maximum fee

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7222Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7222 — Client reschedules a visit from the portal

  Assumes `PortalLive.Visit` at `/portal/visits/:id` exposes a
  reschedule form (`[data-test='reschedule-form']`, fields
  `visit[date]` and `visit[start_time]`) that updates the visit's own
  schedule in place.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a client reschedules an upcoming visit from the portal" do
    scenario "client reschedules a visit from the portal" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have an upcoming visit well within the notice window", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
            start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I reschedule it to a new date and time", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        visit_live
        |> form("[data-test='reschedule-form']",
          visit: %{date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "14:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :visit_live, visit_live)}
      end

      then_ "the visit shows the new date and time", context do
        assert render(context.visit_live) =~ "2:00 PM"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7223Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7223 — Late cancellation shows fee before confirming

  Assumes `PortalLive.Visit` exposes a two-step cancel control (never
  a native `data-confirm` dialog, which `LiveViewTest` can't drive):
  clicking `[data-test='cancel-visit-button']` reveals a
  `[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']` alongside
  `[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']` before anything is cancelled.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "cancelling within the notice window shows the late fee before the client confirms" do
    scenario "late cancellation shows fee before confirming" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the account has a 48-hour notice policy with a $25 late fee", context do
        Fixtures.cancellation_policy_fixture(context.scope, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      given_ "I have a visit scheduled for tomorrow, inside the notice window", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 1),
            start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I start cancelling the visit", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        visit_live
        |> element("[data-test='cancel-visit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :visit_live, visit_live)}
      end

      then_ "I see the late cancellation fee before I confirm", context do
        assert has_element?(context.visit_live, "[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']", "$25.00")
        assert has_element?(context.visit_live, "[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7224Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7224 — On-time cancellation has no fee

  Assumes the same two-step cancel control as criterion 7223's spec:
  `[data-test='cancel-visit-button']` then
  `[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']`, with no
  `[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']` rendered when the visit is
  outside the notice window.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "cancelling outside the notice window charges no fee" do
    scenario "on-time cancellation has no fee" do

  Criterion 7227 — Cannot modify a completed visit

  Assumes `PortalLive.Visit` omits the reschedule form and cancel
  button entirely for a completed visit, rather than rendering them
  disabled.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a completed visit offers no reschedule or cancel controls in the portal" do
    scenario "cannot modify a completed visit" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have a visit that has already been completed", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)
        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I open that visit in the portal", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :visit_live, visit_live)}
      end

      then_ "there is no way to reschedule or cancel it", context do
        refute has_element?(context.visit_live, "[data-test='reschedule-form']")
        refute has_element?(context.visit_live, "[data-test='cancel-visit-button']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7229Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7229 — Same-day cancellation charges the maximum fee

  Assumes the same two-step cancel control as criteria 7223/7224:
  `[data-test='cancel-visit-button']` then
  `[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']`, and that a completed
  same-day cancellation shows the charged fee via
  `[data-test='cancellation-fee-charged']`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "cancelling a visit the same day charges the policy's maximum fee" do
    scenario "same-day cancellation charges the maximum fee" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the account has a $25 late fee and a $50 same-day maximum fee", context do
        Fixtures.cancellation_policy_fixture(context.scope, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      given_ "I have a visit scheduled for later today", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[18:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[20:00:00]
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I cancel the visit and confirm", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        visit_live
        |> element("[data-test='cancel-visit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        assert has_element?(visit_live, "[data-test='cancellation-fee-notice']", "$50.00")

        visit_live
        |> element("[data-test='confirm-cancel-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :visit_live, visit_live)}
      end

      then_ "the maximum same-day fee is charged", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.visit_live,
                 "[data-test='cancellation-fee-charged']",
                 "$50.00"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

input.title: Portal visit page shows "Cleaner: Not yet assigned" for a cleaner who IS assigned but has no name set
input.description:
`CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.Visit.cleaner_name/1` (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/portal_live/visit.ex:167-168):

```elixir
defp cleaner_name(%{cleaner: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name
defp cleaner_name(_job), do: "Not yet assigned"
```

This only matches a cleaner's `name` field being a binary. When a job has a real `cleaner_id` assigned but that cleaner user's `name` column is blank/nil (e.g. `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test`, id 2, which has an email but no name -- a realistic state for any cleaner who hasn't completed their profile), the guard clause fails and falls through to the catch-all, displaying "Cleaner: Not yet assigned" -- indistinguishable from a visit that genuinely has no cleaner assigned at all.

Reproduced: job `bbde8f4e-2823-46ce-ad81-6683882957b3` with `cleaner_id=2` (name nil) showed "Cleaner: Not yet assigned" on `/portal/visits/bbde8f4e-2823-46ce-ad81-6683882957b3`. Reassigning the same job to `cleaner_id=3` (Alex Morgan QA1, which has a name) immediately showed "Cleaner: Alex Morgan QA1" correctly -- confirming the nil-name fallback, not a missing preload, is the cause.

This directly undermines this story's own stated trust goal (knowing who is coming to your home) -- a client would reasonably read "Not yet assigned" as "nobody is scheduled yet" and be surprised when a cleaner shows up. `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.Home.cleaner_identity/1` (story 850) handles this correctly by checking `%{cleaner: nil}` (whether a cleaner is assigned at all) rather than whether the assigned cleaner happens to have a name, falling back to "?" initials -- `PortalLive.Visit` should follow the same pattern instead of conflating "no cleaner" with "cleaner has no display name".

content.text: Another instance of the same class of bug — the portal's reschedule form also accepts a past date with zero validation. Let me confirm this persisted to the database.

input.command: PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h localhost -d cleaner_crm_dev -c "select id, scheduled_date, start_time, status from jobs where id = 'bbde8f4e-2823-46ce-ad81-6683882957b3';"
input.description: Verify the past-date reschedule persisted

input.title: Portal self-service reschedule accepts a past date with no validation
input.description:
`/portal/visits/:id`'s `[data-test='reschedule-form']` accepts any date, including a date years in the past, with no validation error. Submitted `visit[date]=2020-01-01` on job `bbde8f4e-2823-46ce-ad81-6683882957b3` (today is 2026-07-08) and it was accepted and persisted: `select scheduled_date, status from jobs where id=...` shows `scheduled_date=2020-01-01, status='scheduled'` -- a "scheduled" job dated 6 years in the past.

This is the same class of defect as issue 4e985412 (booking-acceptance slot form accepting past dates), which was fixed by adding `validate_slot_in_future/2` to `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_changeset/3`. That fix does not cover this code path: `CleanerCrm.Portal.reschedule_visit/3` (lib/cleaner_crm/portal.ex:127-150) calls `Scheduling.update_job/3` directly with the parsed date/time and has no future-date check anywhere in its `with` chain (`ensure_modifiable/1` only checks status, not date).

# QA Story 852: Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want to view and pay invoices in the portal, manage my card on file, and add a digital tip that reaches my cleaner, so that payment never needs a phone call and tipping doesn't need cash. (Research: over half of tips are digital and incumbents track tips poorly — an in-portal tip prompt is a customer convenience and a cleaner-retention lever — customer-side.md §1; owner-side payment pains pain-points §1.8)

## Acceptance criteria

- Client views invoice list
- Client pays an invoice with a new card
- Invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation
- Declined card leaves invoice unpaid
- Client saves a card on file
- Client adds a tip at payment
- Client pays without tipping

# Qa Story Brief

Per-story QA testing brief. Written by the QA planner after reading the story's prompt file and the QA plan. Gives the tester exact instructions — tool, auth, seeds, what to test.

## Required Sections

### Tool

Format:

- `web` for LiveView pages, `curl` or script path for controller/API routes

### Seeds

### What To Test

## Optional Sections

## Findings and done signal

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__create_issue` **as you find it** — not
written into a markdown file. Capture the title, severity, scope, and a
short description; the call returns an issue id. Hold those ids.

When you finish the session, call
`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured
scenarios payload **and** every issue id you filed:

    mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result(
      task_id: <task_id>,
      status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
      scenarios: [%{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."}, ...],
      issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue>]
    )

Discipline:

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7237Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7237 — Client views invoice list

  Assumes `PortalLive.Invoices` at `/portal/invoices` renders one row
  per invoice (`[data-test='invoice-row-<id>']`) showing its amount
  and paid/unpaid status. This story's other criteria (7238, 7241,
  7242, 7243) assume the same page also carries an inline payment
  form per unpaid invoice (`[data-test='invoice-<id>-pay-button']`
  revealing `[data-test='invoice-<id>-payment-form']` with
  `payment[card_token]`, `payment[save_card]`, and
  `payment[tip_cents]` fields).
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a client sees every invoice for their account in the portal" do
    scenario "client views invoice list" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have one paid invoice and one unpaid invoice", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        paid_job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        paid_invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, paid_job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :paid
          })

        unpaid_job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        unpaid_invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, unpaid_job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("200.00"),
            status: :unpaid
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           paid_invoice: paid_invoice,
           unpaid_invoice: unpaid_invoice,
           portal_conn: portal_conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "I open my invoices in the portal", context do
        {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/invoices")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoices_live, invoices_live)}
      end

      then_ "I see both invoices with their amounts and statuses", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.invoices_live,
                 "[data-test='invoice-row-#{context.paid_invoice.id}']",
                 "$150.00"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.invoices_live,
                 "[data-test='invoice-row-#{context.paid_invoice.id}']",
                 "Paid"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.invoices_live,
                 "[data-test='invoice-row-#{context.unpaid_invoice.id}']",
                 "$200.00"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.invoices_live,
                 "[data-test='invoice-row-#{context.unpaid_invoice.id}']",
                 "Unpaid"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7238Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7238 — Client pays an invoice with a new card

  Per the payments-stripe ADR (see `CleanerCrm.Billing`'s moduledoc),
  a submitted charge only ever moves an invoice to `:charge_pending`
  — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven (criterion 7239). This
  spec's subject is the submission itself, so it asserts the
  submission's own confirmation and receipt rather than a final
  "Paid" status.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a client pays an invoice with a new card from the portal" do
    scenario "client pays an invoice with a new card" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have an unpaid invoice and no card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: false})
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :unpaid
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, invoice: invoice, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I pay the invoice with a new card", context do
        {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/invoices")

        invoices_live
        |> element("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-pay-button']")
        |> render_click()

        invoices_live
        |> form("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-payment-form']",
          payment: %{card_token: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoices_live, invoices_live)}
      end

      then_ "my payment is submitted for the full invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoices_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a receipt", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7239Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7239 — Invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation

  The charge submission itself is covered by criterion 7238's spec;
  this spec's subject is the webhook-driven final transition, so the
  pending charge is seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` and
  the webhook is posted the same way story 836's criterion 7158
  already proves for the owner-facing invoice.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a portal payment is only marked paid once the provider confirms it" do
    scenario "invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I submitted payment on an invoice and it's awaiting confirmation", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :charge_pending,
            stripe_payment_intent_id: "pi_test_portal_succeeded_123"
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, invoice: invoice, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "the provider confirms the charge succeeded", context do
        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => context.invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id,
              "metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => to_string(context.invoice.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "I see the invoice marked paid in the portal", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/invoices")

        assert html =~ "Paid"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7240Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7240 — Declined card leaves invoice unpaid

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive.Invoices do @moduledoc """ Invoice list and payment: pay an open invoice with a new card (optionally saving it on file) and add a digital tip credited to the visit's assigned cleaner. Route: `/portal/invoices`, behind `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s magic-link session. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Portal` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Portal @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Invoices <:subtitle :if={@client.card_on_file}> Card on file
{Money.format_cents(invoice.amount_cents)} {status_label(invoice.status)}

# Qa Story Brief

## Tool

web (portal LiveViews behind magic-link session); curl for `POST /webhooks/stripe` (unauthenticated `:webhook` pipeline — payment confirmation/decline only arrives this way); psql for verifying `tips` table rows and cleaner earnings isolation.

## Auth

Portal (no password): `http://127.0.0.1:4100/portal/access/qa852paymenttoken1234567890abcd` — client "QA Payment852 Client" (email `qa-payment852@example.com`, `card_on_file: false` initially).

Cleaner (for the tip/no-tip earnings check): `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234` at `/users/log-in`. This cleaner (id 2, display name "QA Cleaner Test") is assigned to the tip and no-tip test jobs.

Owner: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234` — not required for this story but available if cross-checking `/invoices` is useful.

## Seeds

Base seeds already applied. Story-specific data inserted directly via psql (no seed script changes needed, one-off entities):

Client `00dbd290-a4c5-4ab3-9b3d-8681c775c940` with these jobs/invoices, all $150.00 (`agreed_price_cents`/`amount_cents` 15000):

- `b09566b8-610a-4768-bacd-f90024e9f30a` — unpaid, no cleaner. Use for criterion 7238 (pay with new card + receipt email).
- `0149ab79-62a5-489d-9074-0f4486ba96e9` — status `charge_pending`, `stripe_payment_intent_id='pi_test_852_ok'`. Use for criterion 7239 (webhook confirms paid).
- `95d8bf44-67bd-44ba-b71c-c91a6a404558` — status `charge_pending`, `stripe_payment_intent_id='pi_test_852_declined'`. Use for criterion 7240 (webhook declines, stays unpaid).
- `0e28ca43-36ff-49be-983e-c31b2c7aab41` — unpaid, no cleaner. Use for criterion 7241 (save card on file).
- `86b53018-b892-4ec5-ab39-42893138e77b` — unpaid, job assigned to `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test`. Use for criterion 7242 (tip at payment).
- `a8cae918-166a-4e84-a037-8efede2cdfb7` — unpaid, job assigned to the same cleaner. Use for criterion 7243 (pay without tipping) — verify via `select * from tips where invoice_id='a8cae918-...'` (expect zero rows) rather than relying solely on the cleaner's aggregate `/field` pay-period total, since that cleaner has pre-existing earnings from other QA sessions that would muddy an exact-dollar assertion.
- `5ab6500b-7dab-493f-95aa-eb153c23a062` — already `paid`, $200.00. Combine with any of the unpaid ones above for criterion 7237 (view list shows both paid and unpaid with correct amounts/status).

## What To Test

- **View invoice list (7237):** open `/portal/invoices`. Expect `[data-test='invoice-row-5ab6500b-...']` showing "$200.00" and "Paid", and at least one unpaid row showing "$150.00" and "Unpaid".
- **Pay with a new card (7238):** click `[data-test='invoice-b09566b8-...-pay-button']`, submit `[data-test='invoice-b09566b8-...-payment-form']` with just `payment[card_token]=pm_card_visa` (the form hard-codes this as a hidden field — real Stripe Elements capture is deferred, same pattern as story 849's booking flow). Expect the page to reflect the submission (amount shown, status likely "Charge Pending" per the ADR — final "Paid" is webhook-driven, not synchronous). Check `/dev/mailbox` for a receipt email to `qa-payment852@example.com`.
- **Invoice marked paid on webhook (7239):** `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4100/webhooks/stripe -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"payment_intent.succeeded","data":{"object":{"id":"pi_test_852_ok","metadata":{"invoice_id":"0149ab79-62a5-489d-9074-0f4486ba96e9"}}}}'`. Reload `/portal/invoices` — expect that row now shows "Paid".
- **Declined card leaves invoice unpaid (7240):** `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4100/webhooks/stripe -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"payment_intent.payment_failed","data":{"object":{"id":"pi_test_852_declined","metadata":{"invoice_id":"95d8bf44-67bd-44ba-b71c-c91a6a404558"}}}}'`. Reload — expect that row still shows "Unpaid" with its pay-button still present (client can retry).
- **Save a card on file (7241):** pay invoice `0e28ca43-...` with `payment[save_card]=true` alongside the card token. Expect `[data-test='card-on-file-badge']` to appear on the page afterward (client-level, not per-invoice). Verify via psql: `select card_on_file from clients where id='00dbd290-...'` should flip to `true`.
- **Add a tip at payment (7242):** pay invoice `86b53018-...` with `payment[tip_cents]=1000` alongside the card token. Verify via psql: `select amount_cents, cleaner_id from tips where invoice_id='86b53018-...'` shows one row, `amount_cents=1000`, `cleaner_id=2`. Then log in as `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test`, visit `/field`, and confirm `[data-test='pay-period-total']` reflects a nonzero total consistent with the added tip (exact aggregate may include other QA data — the psql row is the precise assertion).
- **Pay without tipping (7243):** pay invoice `a8cae918-...` leaving `payment[tip_cents]` blank. Verify via psql that `select count(*) from tips where invoice_id='a8cae918-...'` is 0 — no tip record created for this payment.
- Explore: try submitting a tip of `0` or a negative value; try paying an invoice that's already `paid` (no pay-button should exist to even attempt this); mobile spot-check `/portal/invoices` at 390x844 (expect the already-tracked shared-header overflow, don't refile).

## Result Path

Findings are filed via `create_issue` as discovered; final record is the `submit_qa_result` DB attempt (task id `f502a00a-d93f-4869-a16b-79a0498195df`). Screenshots: `.code_my_spec/qa/852/screenshots/`.

# QA Story 853: Leave a review when the job is done well

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning client, I want a thank-you note after my cleaning with a low-friction review prompt (and a private complaint path if I'm unhappy), so that praising a great cleaner is effortless and problems reach the owner before they reach Google. (Research: Housecall Pro's auto thank-you + ~24h delayed review request is its single most-praised cleaning feature, yielding 2–3x review growth — customer-side.md §4)

## Acceptance criteria

- Thank-you sent on job completion
- Review request sent ~24h after completion
- No duplicate review request
- High rating routes to publish
- Low rating routes to private complaint
- Owner receives private complaint
- No review prompt for incomplete visit

## BDD spec files

- `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7244_thank-you_sent_on_job_completion_spex.exs`
- `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7245_review_request_sent_24h_after_completion_spex.exs`
- `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7246_no_duplicate_review_request_spex.exs`

- `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7248_low_rating_routes_to_private_complaint_spex.exs`

- `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm/test/spex/853_leave_a_review_when_the_job_is_done_well/criterion_7250_no_review_prompt_for_incomplete_visit_spex.exs`

- Tests: `test/cleaner_crm_web/live/review_live_test.exs`
